question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Harry stepped in, his head almost ______ the sloping ceiling, and blinked.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. touching.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Touching means coming into contact with something, usually lightly. (छूना / स्पर्श करना)

◦ The sentence describes a tall person entering a room with a low sloping ceiling — his head very nearly comes into contact with it, so "almost touching" is the natural collocation.

◦ Correct: Harry stepped in, his head almost touching the sloping ceiling, and blinked.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Embracing" means hugging someone warmly or accepting an idea — a ceiling cannot be embraced by a head.

• "Grasping" means seizing something firmly with the hand, which a head cannot do.

• "Cuddling" means holding someone close affectionately, which is unsuitable for an inanimate ceiling.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: touch the sky, touch a nerve, keep in touch, a touching story (moving).

• "Embrace" also has a figurative sense: *She embraced the new technology* (accepted it willingly).

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correctly spelt words.
option_1: I was a bit depressed by our apparant lack of progress.
option_2: Urban dwellers often accept noise as part of city life.
option_3: She is going to divorce him on the grounds of adultary.
option_4: Its sanctions are based on compairisons between the two companies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Urban dwellers often accept noise as part of city life.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 2 — *urban, dwellers, accept, noise* — is correctly spelt, so it is the only error-free sentence. (नगरवासी)

◦ Note the pair accept (to receive/agree) vs except (other than); the sentence uses "accept" correctly.

◦ Correct: Urban dwellers often accept noise as part of city life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "apparant" is wrong; the correct spelling is apparent (spelt with -ent).

• Option 3: "adultary" is wrong; the correct spelling is adultery (extramarital relations).

• Option 4: "compairisons" is wrong; the correct spelling is comparisons (no 'i' after 'a').

NOTE

• Frequently misspelt SSC words: occurrence, embarrass, maintenance, privilege, separate, definitely, harass.

• Do not confuse adultery (infidelity) with adulteration (mixing impurities in food).

question: Four words are given, out of which three words are spelt correctly. Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. VISCIOUS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is VICIOUS (V-I-C-I-O-U-S), meaning cruel, violent or savage. (क्रूर / हिंसक)

◦ The printed form "VISCIOUS" wrongly inserts an 's' — it appears to blend *vicious* with *viscous* (thick and sticky).

◦ Correct: The dog gave him a vicious bite.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "STILETTOS" is correct — women's shoes with very high thin heels (also a slender dagger).

• "BEWILDERS" is correct — puzzles or confuses someone completely.

• "UNFORESEEN" is correct — not anticipated or predicted in advance.

NOTE

• Distinguish vicious (cruel) from viscous (thick liquid, like honey) — both are asked in SSC spelling sets.

• Common idiom: a vicious circle — a situation in which one problem causes another, which worsens the first.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A historical account or biography written from personal knowledge
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Memoir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A memoir is a historical account or biography written from personal knowledge or special sources — a record of one's own experiences. (संस्मरण)

◦ The key element in the definition is *personal knowledge*, which points precisely to "memoir".

◦ Correct: Her memoir of the war years became a bestseller.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Chronicle" — a factual record of events arranged in order of time, not necessarily personal.

• "Thesis" — a long research dissertation submitted for an academic degree.

• "Blog" — a regularly updated website or web page written in an informal, conversational style.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: Autobiography (life story written by oneself), Biography (life story written by another), Diary (daily personal record), Anthology (collection of poems/stories).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

Though they allow celebrities and famous people to take pictures (inside the museum, but they does not allow the general public) to do the same.
option_1: inside the museum, they do not allow the general public
option_3: inside the museum, but do not allowing the general public
option_4: inside the museum, they does not allow general public
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. inside the museum, they do not allow the general public.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence already begins with the subordinating conjunction "Though", so adding "but" in the main clause is a double conjunction error. Use one connector, not two. (दोहरा संयोजक अशुद्धि)

◦ The plural pronoun "they" takes the plural verb "do", never "does"; also "the general public" needs the definite article the.

◦ Correct: Though they allow celebrities and famous people to take pictures inside the museum, they do not allow the general public to do the same.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is wrong because the bracketed part has both a "though…but" error and a subject-verb agreement error.

• Option 3 "but do not allowing" is wrong — "do not" must be followed by the bare infinitive "allow", not "allowing".

• Option 4 keeps the wrong verb "does" with "they" and drops the article before "general public".

NOTE

• Never pair these: Though/Although…but, Because…so, As…therefore, Unless…not.

• Correct: *Although he was tired, he finished the work* (no "but").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

I assisted him to undo the (task after I finished my work).
option_1: task after I will finish my work
option_3: task after I will have finished my work
option_4: task after I had finished my work
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. task after I had finished my work.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When two past actions are described, the earlier action takes the past perfect (had + V3) and the later action takes the simple past. (पूर्ण भूतकाल)

◦ Here "finishing my work" happened before "assisting him", so it must be had finished, while the main verb "assisted" stays in the simple past.

◦ Correct: I assisted him to undo the task after I had finished my work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "will finish" mixes a future tense with the past verb "assisted" — a tense-sequence error.

• Option 2 is wrong because the simple past "finished" fails to show that the action was completed earlier.

• Option 3 "will have finished" is future perfect and again clashes with the past main clause.

NOTE

• Rule of past perfect: had + V3 for the first of two past actions; often with *after, before, when, by the time*.

• Example: *The train had left before we reached the station.*

question:
Select the word from the options which is exactly opposite in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

The pandemic has seen soaring home prices and record housing (insecurity).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Firmness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Insecurity means a lack of stability, safety or confidence — a state of uncertainty. (असुरक्षा / अस्थिरता)

• Firmness means steadiness, stability and resolute confidence, which is exactly the opposite of insecurity. (दृढ़ता / स्थिरता)

◦ Correct: The pandemic has seen soaring home prices and record housing insecurity; the antonym of the bracketed word is firmness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Hesitancy" means reluctance or wavering — a synonym, not an antonym, of insecurity.

• "Pretence" means a false show or make-believe; it is unrelated to the idea of stability.

• "Self-doubt" means lack of confidence in oneself — again close in meaning to insecurity.

NOTE

• Synonyms of insecurity: instability, vulnerability, anxiety, uncertainty, precariousness.

• Synonyms of firmness: steadfastness, resolve, solidity, determination, stability.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Eight years ago, she founded / Humans of Bombay, inspired of / the single idea – we all want to be heard.
option_1: the single idea – we all want to be heard.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Humans of Bombay, inspired of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "inspire" takes the preposition by when it names the source of the inspiration — *inspired by something/someone*, never "inspired of". (प्रेरित होना)

◦ "Inspired" here is a past participle used as a reduced passive; the agent after a passive participle is introduced by by.

◦ Correct: Eight years ago, she founded Humans of Bombay, inspired by the single idea – we all want to be heard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Eight years ago, she founded" is correct — "ago" is properly used with the simple past.

• Option 1 "the single idea – we all want to be heard." is correct — the dash introduces an explanatory clause.

• Option 3 is wrong because the sentence does contain a preposition error.

NOTE

• Fixed prepositions: inspired by, influenced by, accompanied by, surrounded by, impressed by/with.

• But note: inspiration for something, and inspired to + verb (*She was inspired to write*).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

The branch of physics concerned with the properties of sound
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Acoustics.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Acoustics is the branch of physics that deals with sound — its production, transmission and effects. (ध्वनि विज्ञान)

◦ It also refers to the sound quality of a hall: *The acoustics of the auditorium are excellent.*

◦ Correct: Acoustics is the branch of physics concerned with the properties of sound.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Anchor" — a heavy device that keeps a ship in place, or a person who presents a TV programme.

• "Anarchist" — a person who believes government and law should be abolished.

• "Apiary" — a place where bees are kept for their honey.

NOTE

• Related branches: Optics (light), Entomology (insects), Ornithology (birds), Seismology (earthquakes), Numismatics (coins).

• Related places: Aviary (birds), Apiary (bees), Aquarium (fish), Hive (bee colony).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Satisfactory
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Inadequate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Satisfactory means good enough, acceptable or fulfilling the required standard. (संतोषजनक)

• Inadequate means insufficient or not good enough for the purpose — the exact opposite. (अपर्याप्त)

◦ Correct: His performance was far from satisfactory; in fact it was inadequate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Revive" is a verb meaning to bring back to life or restore; it is not an adjective and cannot be an antonym here.

• "Morose" means gloomy and bad-tempered — the opposite of cheerful, not of satisfactory.

• "Diminish" is a verb meaning to make or become less.

NOTE

• Synonyms of satisfactory: adequate, acceptable, sufficient, passable, up to the mark.

• Other antonyms: unsatisfactory, deficient, substandard, poor, wanting.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Enthuse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fondle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Enthuse means to show or express great excitement and eagerness about something, or to make someone enthusiastic. (उत्साहित करना)

• Of the four choices, only Fondle carries a positive, affectionate feeling; the other three — *unbothered, carefree, lazy* — all suggest indifference or lack of interest, i.e. the opposite of enthusiasm.

◦ Correct (as per the official key): The synonym of "Enthuse" is Fondle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Unbothered" means not worried or not concerned — the antonym of an enthusiastic attitude.

• "Carefree" means free from anxiety or responsibility, which is not the same as being eager.

• "Lazy" means unwilling to work or use energy — clearly opposite to enthusiasm.

NOTE

• True synonyms of enthuse: *rave, gush, be excited about, rhapsodise, motivate, inspire*. Antonyms: *bore, dampen, discourage*.

• The tick in the official answer key is on Option 3 ("Fondle"), so it has been recorded as the answer, although "fondle" (to caress/stroke lovingly) is not a true dictionary synonym of "enthuse" — treat this as a defective SSC item and go with the key.

question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

You all look great in your costumes! (Good luck!)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Break a leg.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Break a leg is a theatrical idiom used to wish a performer good luck before going on stage. (शुभकामनाएँ देना)

◦ The context — people in costumes about to perform — makes this the perfect substitution for "Good luck!".

◦ Correct: You all look great in your costumes! Break a leg!

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Come again" means "please repeat what you said" — a request for repetition.

• "Don't swear it" is not a standard English idiom.

• "Spit it out" means to say what you are hesitating to say, quickly and directly.

NOTE

• Other good-luck expressions: fingers crossed, knock 'em dead, best of luck.

• More stage idioms: steal the show (win all the praise), in the limelight (at the centre of attention), wait in the wings (be ready for one's chance).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A bad egg
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A bad person.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a bad egg" refers to a dishonest, worthless or troublesome person — someone of bad character. (बुरा व्यक्ति)

◦ The opposite idiom is "a good egg", meaning a thoroughly likeable, decent person.

◦ Correct: Don't trust him with the money; he has always been a bad egg.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "A very small insignificant amount" is the meaning of a drop in the ocean, not of "a bad egg".

• "To be frustrated" is expressed by idioms like at one's wits' end or fed up.

• "To calm down" corresponds to cool off or simmer down.

NOTE

• More 'person' idioms: a black sheep (disgrace to the family), a wolf in sheep's clothing (a hidden enemy), a fair-weather friend (a friend only in good times), a big fish (an important person).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Bushfire in Australia has ______ the conditions of many animals in the forest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. worsened.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Worsened means made or become worse — a decline in condition. (बदतर करना / बिगाड़ना)

◦ A bushfire is a destructive event, so it can only make the condition of forest animals worse; the sentence needs a negative-impact verb.

◦ Correct: Bushfire in Australia has worsened the conditions of many animals in the forest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Fortified" means strengthened or reinforced — a positive sense, unsuitable after a disaster.

• "Maintained" means kept in the same state, which contradicts the destructive effect of a fire.

• "Surpassed" means exceeded or went beyond; it does not collocate with "conditions".

NOTE

• Synonyms of worsen: deteriorate, aggravate, exacerbate, decline. Antonyms: improve, ameliorate, better.

• Note the spelling pair: aggravate (make worse) vs irritate (annoy).

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed part given in the sentence below.

I was (feeling afraid) that something bad would happen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Scared.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Scared means frightened or afraid — exactly the sense of the bracketed phrase "feeling afraid". (डरा हुआ)

◦ After the verb "was", an adjective is required, and "scared" fits both the meaning and the grammar.

◦ Correct: I was scared that something bad would happen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Sacred" means holy or connected with religion — a common spelling trap with "scared".

• "Divine" means godlike or heavenly, again unrelated to fear.

• "Bold" means brave and confident, which is the very opposite of feeling afraid.

NOTE

• Synonyms of scared: terrified, frightened, petrified, apprehensive, panic-stricken.

• Watch these look-alike pairs: scared/sacred, desert/dessert, quite/quiet, angle/angel.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Raising temperatures in the springtime signal plants and animals to come alive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Raising temperatures in the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rise" is an intransitive verb (rise – rose – risen) meaning to go up by itself, while "raise" is transitive (raise – raised – raised) and needs an object. (स्वयं बढ़ना बनाम बढ़ाना)

◦ Temperatures go up on their own, so the participial adjective must be rising, not "raising".

◦ Correct: Rising temperatures in the springtime signal plants and animals to come alive.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "springtime signal plants and" is correct — the plural verb "signal" agrees with the plural subject "temperatures".

• Option 3 "animals to come alive." is correct — "signal + object + to-infinitive" is a standard structure.

• Option 4 is wrong because the sentence does contain an error in the first part.

NOTE

• Similar transitive/intransitive pairs: lie (lay, lain) vs lay (laid, laid); sit vs set; fall vs fell.

• Correct usage: *The sun rises in the east*; *He raised his hand*.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There was a general hesitation and ______ to ignore the problem.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Demur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Demur as a noun means hesitation, objection or reluctance; as a verb it means to raise doubts or object. (आपत्ति / हिचकिचाहट)

◦ The blank is joined by "and" to the noun "hesitation", so it needs a noun of similar meaning — "demur" fits both grammatically and in sense.

◦ Correct: There was a general hesitation and demur to ignore the problem.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Disposition" means a person's natural temperament or an inclination — an inclination *to ignore* would contradict "hesitation".

• "Deride" is a verb meaning to mock or ridicule, so it cannot follow "hesitation and".

• "Denigrate" is also a verb, meaning to criticise unfairly or belittle someone.

NOTE

• Common phrase: without demur — without objecting or hesitating (*He agreed without demur*).

• Synonyms of demur: objection, protest, reservation, qualm, misgiving.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Look in a mirror and take your ______ with each step.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Take your time is a fixed idiomatic phrase meaning to do something slowly and carefully, without hurrying. (जल्दबाज़ी न करना)

◦ The possessive "your" before the blank signals the idiom "take one's time"; the advice to watch each step in a mirror supports this sense.

◦ Correct: Look in a mirror and take your time with each step.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Plague" means a deadly epidemic disease or, as a verb, to trouble someone constantly — it does not fit "take your ___".

• "Ages" means a very long time, but "take your ages" is not idiomatic English ("it takes ages" is).

• "Hostage" means a captive; one takes *someone* hostage, not "your hostage" in this context.

NOTE

• Other "take" idioms: take after (resemble), take off (leave the ground / remove), take up (start a hobby), take to task (scold), take for granted (undervalue).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Have you ever gone into/ a high-street shop wearing/ a pair of cycling shorts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is grammatically sound throughout, so "No error" is the right choice. (कोई त्रुटि नहीं)

◦ Have you ever gone into — the present perfect with "ever" is standard for asking about experience, and "gone into" (entered) takes "into" correctly.

◦ a pair of cycling shorts — plural-only garments (shorts, trousers, jeans, scissors) are counted with "a pair of".

◦ Correct: Have you ever gone into a high-street shop wearing a pair of cycling shorts? — no change needed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "Have you ever gone into" is correct — "gone" is the past participle required after "have".

• Option 2 "a high-street shop wearing" is correct — "wearing" is a participial phrase modifying "you", and the compound adjective "high-street" is properly hyphenated before the noun.

• Option 1 "a pair of cycling shorts?" is correct in both article and number.

NOTE

• Have been to = visited and returned; have gone to = went and is still there — a favourite SSC distinction.

• Always "a pair of" with: spectacles, tongs, pyjamas, binoculars, pliers.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

She was born with full sight and hearing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In "full sight and hearing", the adjective full correctly modifies the two nouns sight and hearing after the preposition "with". (पूर्ण दृष्टि एवं श्रवण-शक्ति)

◦ A preposition must be followed by a noun or noun phrase, and "full sight" is a perfectly formed noun phrase; the parallel noun "hearing" confirms it.

◦ Correct: She was born with full sight and hearing. — no change is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "full sighting" is wrong — "sighting" means the act of spotting something (*a rare bird sighting*), not the sense of vision.

• Option 2 "fully sight" is wrong — the adverb "fully" cannot modify the noun "sight"; adverbs modify verbs/adjectives.

• Option 3 "full sighted" is wrong — "sighted" is an adjective and would not run parallel with the noun "hearing"; the standard adjective is "fully sighted" used before a noun.

NOTE

• Adjective + noun after a preposition: *with great care*, *in full swing*, *at short notice*.

• Related words: sight (vision), sightseeing (visiting places of interest), insight (deep understanding), oversight (an unintentional omission).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. within.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Within is the preposition used before a period of time to mean "before the end of that period" — *within minutes, within a week*. (के भीतर)

◦ The passage says allergies begin to act up very soon after the earrings go in, so "within minutes of putting earrings in your ears" is the natural expression.

◦ Correct: Metal allergies can begin to act up within minutes of putting earrings in your ears.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "of" cannot introduce a time span after "act up"; it would leave the sentence meaningless.

• "about" would mean "approximately", but it does not fit before "minutes of putting".

• "with" indicates accompaniment or means, not a period of time.

NOTE

• Time prepositions: in (a month/year), on (a day/date), at (a clock time), within (before the end of a period), by (not later than).

• Phrasal verb here: act up — to start causing trouble or behaving badly.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. take.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb take out means to remove something from a place — the standard verb used for removing earrings. (निकालना)

◦ The structure "having to ______ the earrings out" needs a bare infinitive after "to", and only "take" forms an idiomatic phrasal verb with the particle "out" here.

◦ Correct: Some people can go a few hours before having to take the earrings out.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Expel" means to force someone to leave a school or country, or to drive something out forcefully — too strong and wrong in register.

• "Make … out" means to manage to see or understand something, which does not suit removing jewellery.

• "Hand out" means to distribute something to a group of people.

NOTE

• Useful "take" phrasal verbs: take off (remove/leave the ground), take in (absorb/deceive), take over (assume control), take back (retract).

• Separable phrasal verbs allow both "take out the earrings" and "take the earrings out".

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. discomfort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Discomfort means slight pain or physical uneasiness — precisely what a metal allergy causes. (असुविधा / तकलीफ़)

◦ The collocation "stand the discomfort" (= endure the irritation) fits the contrast introduced by "but some can barely…".

◦ Correct: … but some can barely stand the discomfort enough to bother putting earrings in at all.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "bomb" is an explosive device and has no connection with an allergic reaction.

• "knife" is a cutting tool; the passage describes irritation, not injury by a blade.

• "burn" refers to an injury from fire or heat — an allergy causes itching and soreness, not a burn.

NOTE

• Here stand = tolerate/endure, as in *I can't stand the noise*.

• Synonyms of discomfort: uneasiness, irritation, soreness, distress, inconvenience.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. who.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relative pronoun who is used for people and functions as the subject of the relative clause. (कर्ता के लिए प्रयुक्त संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम)

◦ In "those of us ______ love to wear earrings", the blank is the subject of the verb "love", and the antecedent "us" refers to persons — so who is required.

◦ Correct: This can be discouraging for those of us who love to wear earrings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "whom" is the object form of "who"; here the pronoun is the subject, so "whom" is wrong.

• "which" is used only for things and animals, not for people.

• "that" cannot be used after the pattern "those of us", which idiomatically takes "who".

NOTE

• Quick test: replace with he/him — if he fits, use who; if him fits, use whom.

• Relative pronouns: who/whom (persons), which (things), whose (possession), that (persons or things, defining clauses only).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sensitive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sensitive means easily affected or irritated — the standard word used for skin or body parts that react to metals or chemicals. (संवेदनशील)

◦ Hypoallergenic jewellery is specifically designed for people with allergies, so it is made for sensitive ears.

◦ Correct: … but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for sensitive ears exists!

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "rustic" means rural or countryside-like in style; it cannot describe ears.

• "soft" describes texture and does not convey the idea of an allergic reaction.

• "modern" means belonging to the present time and has no link with allergies.

NOTE

• Hypoallergenic = designed to cause the fewest possible allergic reactions (*hypo-* = under/less).

• Do not confuse sensitive (easily affected emotionally/physically) with sensible (having good judgement) — a very common SSC confusable pair.
